key_insight: LLM-simulated clients show both similarities and differences to human role-players in counselling communication patterns, suggesting potential for training without establishing equivalence.
engineering_relevance: Virtual counselling clients could support training systems, but their conversational patterns should be evaluated against human role-play before deployment.
method: Record novice counsellors interacting with human peers acting as clients.
Conduct human–LLM role-plays using Mixtral 8x7B with 4-bit quantization.
Analyse sentence-level counselling patterns and compare interactions across client types.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports similarities and differences across human-client and LLM-client sessions but provides no sample sizes, effect sizes, or quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether observed conversational similarities translate into improved counselling competencies.
paper_title: Comparing Human Role-Players and LLM-Simulated Clients in Online Counselling Training: An Analysis of Counselling Patterns
